entries.phase_name: Honest Plan Orchestration Across Go and TypeScript
entries.description: TypeScript lifecycle planning currently marks plan dispatches completed and supplies a synthetic top-level phase_plan without explicit synthesis provenance, so a completion file can look like real worker evidence when no planning workers ran.
entries.suggestion: Remove fake completed planning dispatches or introduce an explicit synthesis envelope; add TS tests that capture and parse the plan-finalize completion file.

entries.phase_name: Honest Plan Orchestration Across Go and TypeScript
entries.description: plan-finalize accepts completion-level phase_plan before proving it came from route-setter evidence or an explicit synthesis contract, allowing ambiguous host-generated plans to mutate COLONY_STATE.json.
entries.suggestion: Require route_setter-owned embedded or freshly claimed phase_plan for real-worker mode; reject completed worker claims paired only with a top-level phase_plan unless explicit synthesis mode is present.

entries.phase_name: Honest Plan Orchestration Across Go and TypeScript
entries.description: A generic root mismatch helper exists, but Phase 2 still needs a plan-finalize-specific regression proving mismatched plan_manifest.root leaves COLONY_STATE.json unchanged.
entries.suggestion: Add a codex_plan_finalize test using a manifest from a different temp root and assert root mismatch plus unchanged state.

entries.phase_name: Honest Plan Orchestration Across Go and TypeScript
entries.description: Freshness and workspace checks exist, but missing phase_plan, empty phases, no buildable tasks, and ambiguous synthetic worker completion are not covered as one finalizer contract boundary.
entries.suggestion: Add unchanged-state tests for missing phase_plan, empty phase_plan.phases, empty tasks, stale claimed phase-plan, and ambiguous top-level synthetic phase_plan.

entries.phase_name: Honest Plan Orchestration Across Go and TypeScript
entries.description: Platform subprocesses inherit the process environment and collect provider stdout/stderr; Go bridge redaction exists, but planning dispatch changes must not surface raw provider auth output.
entries.suggestion: Preserve existing redaction tests and add provider-output tests if planning starts invoking platform subprocesses.

entries.phase_name: Research, Guided Rituals, and Read-Only Dashboards
entries.description: TS Oracle lifecycle synthesizes current_confidence from worker success and submits it to oracle-iterate-finalize; Go finalizer persists completion.CurrentConfidence, so dashboards can report invented research confidence.
entries.suggestion: Move confidence calculation and validation into Go, or reject externally supplied confidence unless it is derived from validated worker evidence.

entries.phase_name: Research, Guided Rituals, and Read-Only Dashboards
entries.description: normalizeOracleWorkerResponse fills a default blocked summary before checking for blocker detail, so a blocked response with no findings or gaps can pass with a generic blocker.
entries.suggestion: Validate blocked responses before applying a default summary, and require concrete gaps, findings, or recommendation text for blocked status.

entries.phase_name: Research, Guided Rituals, and Read-Only Dashboards
entries.description: status is documented as read-only, but the error path calls renderRecoveryMenu, which emits a loop-break event through the event bus and can mutate .aether/data on failed dashboard reads.
entries.suggestion: Suppress recovery event emission for read-only dashboards or document the error-path event-bus write in the status contract.

entries.phase_name: Research, Guided Rituals, and Read-Only Dashboards
entries.description: watch is described as read-only monitoring and lists watch-snapshot.json, but the implementation writes watch-status.txt and watch-progress.txt artifacts instead.
entries.suggestion: Update the watch contract to name the actual Go-owned artifacts and state that watch is monitoring-only but artifact-writing.

entries.phase_name: Delivery, Internal Commands, and Release Verification
entries.description: npm audit is clean for .aether/ts-host and .aether/ts but not for .opencode.

porter --full-release captures CombinedOutput from release commands run with the inherited environment and stores/prints the last output lines without applying the existing credential redaction path. A failed npm/go/goreleaser command that emits API keys or tokens could leak them into porter readiness evidence and user-visible output.
entries.suggestion: Apply codex.SanitizeWorkerDiagnosticOutput or an equivalent redactor before assigning integrityCheck.Message for release/test command failures, add regression coverage with token-shaped output, and consider minimizing the inherited environment for release command checks.

entries.description: npm audit for the npm package could not run because the package has no lockfile; it currently declares no dependencies, so no npm package vulnerability finding was identified from that manifest.
entries.suggestion: Keep the npm package dependency-free or add and commit a lockfile before adding dependencies so audit coverage remains available.

entries.phase_name: Seal Evidence and Delivery Readiness Cleanup
entries.description: Full-release command failures store raw trailing command output in the check message, and the readiness result is persisted to .aether/data/porter/readiness.json; release tool output can contain auth/provider details or secrets.
entries.suggestion: Redact secret-like values and sensitive provider output before rendering or persisting porter command failure messages.

entries.description: Previous HIGH blocker resolved: Porter failed-command snippets are passed through codex.SanitizeWorkerDiagnosticOutput before being shown or persisted in readiness evidence.
Full-release readiness receipt is critical only because Git status reports 84 uncommitted changes; no skipped checks were present and release/tool verification checks passed.

runPorterCommandCheck assigns failure Message from lastPorterOutputLines, and lastPorterOutputLines sanitizes the final diagnostic lines before returning them. Focused token-shaped regression tests passed locally.
entries.suggestion: Keep the token-shaped redaction regression tests in cmd/porter_cmd_test.go active for future porter changes.

entries.description: The canonical review artifact still lists the prior porter redaction blocker even though the source and focused tests now show the issue fixed. This leaves the security evidence contradictory.
entries.suggestion: Regenerate the phase review artifact after the fix so the security ledger and continue evidence reflect the current source state.

entries.description: Current source routes failed Porter command output through codex.SanitizeWorkerDiagnosticOutput before storing or rendering failure messages, addressing the earlier raw-output leak path.
entries.suggestion: Keep token-shaped regression coverage around lastPorterOutputLines and runPorterCommandCheck.

entries.description: OSV module-version scan reports advisories in unneeded Go module graph entries: GHSA-xmrv-pmrh-hhx2, CVE-2025-47914, CVE-2025-58181, CVE-2025-47913, CVE-2025-47911, CVE-2025-58190, CVE-2026-33814, and CVE-2026-33186. go mod why -m reports the main module does not need the affected modules, and go list -deps ./cmd/aether showed no affected packages in the built CLI dependency set.
entries.suggestion: Run govulncheck when available and consider a dependency tidy/update pass to remove stale advisory-bearing module graph entries.

However, loadFreshSealFinalReview checks freshness and gate satisfaction before checking the own report phase, so a future passed stale report from a different phase could be reused if it is still fresh.
